# Root reconstruction of exact ideal singleton minimax and its boundaries

2026-10-16. Internal analytic reconstruction of the construction in gc_peak_genesis, following a separate fixed-grid receiving deduction by gc_control_adversary. Random refresh/DD protocols are established primary prior art from2005. No new hardware, practical threshold or historical originality is claimed.

## Model and exact question

Choose N public deterministic refresh slots before the Hamiltonian is selected. An independent fair private bit toggles the frame at each slot; an initial private uniform frame and exact final tracked inverse are supplied. Every complete process, seed independence/coarse graining, covariance and support promise is retained. In virtual seed coordinates the fixed slots apply complete parity pinching, without acquiring a physical syndrome detector or observing a latent outcome. A fixed Hamiltonian may depend on public slots but may not read the private bits. It includes an arbitrary finite shared bath and syndrome-preserving baseline; its own parity-changing term has norm bounded by a known integrable j(t).

Let a_k be the action in gap k, m=N+1. For the singleton final odd-character effect, the exact worstcase over this admitted model is

    Q(a_1,...,a_m)=1-product_k cos^2(min(a_k,pi/2)).

For fixed total action a, the best public slot placement has equal-action gaps and minimax value

    Q_N(a)=1-cos^(2(N+1))(min(a/(N+1),pi/2)).

This is a singleton result. The previously proved shared-bath all-subset product of squared gap actions remains the receiving theorem for joint events. A product of singleton sine improvements is not asserted without a separate proof.

## Upper bound

In the interaction picture of the syndrome-preserving baseline, the subspace-angle bound gives ||P_minus U P_plus||<=sin(min(a_k,pi/2)).
